Moving costs

How much do movers cost?

Use the free calculator below to see how much do movers cost for your home and route. It takes about a minute and needs no email.

20+ years in the moving business

  • Home or apartment

Where are you moving?

Two ZIP codes give us the distance and the type of move.

Estimator's noteShort moves are usually billed by the hour for the crew and truck. Long moves are priced by the weight of your things and the distance. Your ZIP codes decide which applies.

Your price shows before we ask for any contact details.

Local movers cost $280–$740 for a studio apartment and $1,800–$4,300 for a home of 4 or more bedrooms, at 10 road miles, off peak, with no stairs or extras. That is how much do movers cost for a local move, billed by the hour for a crew and a truck. Long-distance movers price by weight and miles instead: a 2-bedroom home moved 1,000 miles costs $2,600–$5,700 on the same terms.

How much do movers cost, by home size

When you ask how much do movers cost, the number of bedrooms is the quickest guide, because movers size up a job by what's in your home. The table gives the range for each home size from the rate table behind the calculator. Local prices are for 10 road miles and long-distance prices for 1,000 road miles. Both assume an off-peak date, no stairs and no extras such as packing or storage.

Home sizeLocal move, 10 milesLong-distance move, 1,000 miles
Studio apartment$280–$740$1,150–$2,350
1-bedroom home$380–$960$1,400–$3,300
2-bedroom home$720–$1,800$2,600–$5,700
3-bedroom home$1,150–$2,850$4,000–$8,550
4 or more bedrooms$1,800–$4,300$5,700–$11,800

The ranges are wide because two homes with the same number of bedrooms can hold very different amounts of furniture and boxes, and each moving company sets its own rates. Enter your ZIP codes in the calculator above for a range that fits your move.

Moving only a few pieces rather than a whole home? A local move of 1 to 3 items costs $180–$590 at 10 road miles, off peak, with no stairs or extras.

Local moves: you pay for the crew's time

On a local move, how much do movers cost comes down to two numbers: the crew's hourly rate and the hours the job takes. An hourly rate on its own tells you little until you know the crew size and the hours.

Take a 2-bedroom home. It usually needs 3 movers, and their rate together is $150–$225 an hour, which is $50–$75 an hour for each mover, truck included. The whole move costs $720–$1,800 at 10 road miles, off peak, with no stairs and no extras. The crew table below shows how the hours and the total shift with each crew size.

Because you pay for time, anything that slows the crew raises the price: flights of stairs, an elevator shared with other residents, a long walk from the door to the truck, or packing that isn't finished when the crew arrives. A longer drive adds time too, so the same move at 30 miles costs more than at 10. Before you book, ask when the clock starts and stops, whether travel time to your home is billed, and whether there is a minimum number of hours.

Long-distance moves: weight, miles and a delivery window

Once a move crosses state lines or covers hundreds of miles, the hours matter less, and how much do movers cost rests on how much your shipment weighs, or how much room it takes in the truck, and how far it travels. Interstate movers are regulated by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA).

The same 2-bedroom home moved 1,000 road miles costs $2,600–$5,700, off peak, with no stairs and no extras. Spread over the distance, that works out to about $2.60–$5.70 per mile. That figure is the total divided by the miles, not a rate movers bill by.

Long-distance movers usually give a delivery window, a span of days, rather than one delivery date. Get the window in writing with the estimate.

Binding and non-binding estimates

Federal rules require an interstate mover to give you a written estimate of all charges, and a mover's "rate quote" is not an estimate. FMCSA advises that the estimate be based on an in-person or video inspection of your goods. With a binding estimate, you pay no more than the estimated amount at delivery. If you add items or services, or conditions such as stairs or a parking permit come up, the mover must write a new binding estimate. With a non-binding estimate, the mover can't require you to pay more than 110 percent of the estimate at delivery. FMCSA explains both kinds of estimate.

What changes how much do movers cost

Size and distance set the range for how much do movers cost. These details decide where in that range your move lands, and they explain most of the gap between two movers' prices for the same home.

  • How much you own. More furniture and boxes mean more movers, a bigger truck and more hours on a local move, and more weight on a long-distance one.
  • Your moving date. Summer, weekends and the end of the month are the busiest times for movers. In the rate table behind the calculator, a July date raises both ends of the range for the same 2-bedroom, 1,000-mile move.
  • Stairs and access. Full flights of stairs raise the price, and so can a long carry from the door to the truck, an elevator you have to book, or a street where the truck needs a parking permit.
  • Packing. Having the movers pack adds a packing charge that grows with the size of your home. If you pack yourself, you buy the boxes, tape and paper instead, and the box estimator below counts them room by room.
  • Heavy specialty items. A piano, pool table or hot tub needs extra hands or equipment and is priced on its own. Moving an upright piano locally costs $220–$490 at 10 road miles, off peak, with no stairs or extras.
  • Storage and car shipping. Both are priced on top of the move itself.

Hiring movers or a DIY move

A DIY move swaps how much do movers cost for your own time, effort and risk. A rental truck is billed by the day plus mileage for a move in town, or by the road mile for a one-way rental, with fuel extra, and you load it and drive it. A portable container sits in between: you pack and load, and the container company does the driving.

You can also mix the two and hire labor only, a crew that loads and unloads a truck you rent. The comparison below prices this move as a rental truck, a container and full-service movers. Before you choose, add up the truck, mileage, fuel, supplies and days off work.

Ways to bring the price down

Most of what you can do to lower how much do movers cost happens in the weeks before moving day, and the checklist below puts those tasks in order.

  • Move less. Sell, donate or throw out what you won't use before the movers see it. Fewer pieces mean fewer hours on a local move and less weight on a long-distance one.
  • Pick a quieter date. A weekday in the middle of the month, outside summer, avoids the busiest times.
  • Be ready when the crew arrives. Have every box packed, taped and labeled, the beds taken apart, and the parking space and elevator booked, so the crew starts work as soon as it walks in.
  • Do part of the work. Pack your own boxes, carry the small things yourself, or rent a truck and hire labor only for the heavy lifting.
  • Keep the inventory honest. A mover can only price what it knows about. Pieces left off the list at the survey get added on moving day, and so does the cost.

What valuation coverage adds

On an interstate move, valuation is part of how much do movers cost. Interstate movers must offer two levels of liability, which federal rules call valuation. Released value costs nothing extra, but the mover pays no more than $0.60 per pound per article, so a light but valuable item gets little back. Full-value protection makes the mover responsible for the replacement value of lost or damaged goods, and it applies unless you sign for released value. It costs extra and the price varies by mover: published figures put it at $10.00–$20.00 per $1,000 of declared value. FMCSA also notes that damage to boxes you pack yourself may be harder to claim for. Read FMCSA's guide to valuation.

A firm answer to how much do movers cost

An estimate of how much do movers cost stays a range until a mover has seen what you're moving. To close the gap:

  1. Enter your ZIP codes in the calculator above. It's free, takes about a minute and needs no email to see your price.
  2. Ask more than one mover for a written estimate after an in-home or video survey, and give each the same inventory, services and date.
  3. Compare the estimates line by line: crew size and hours, or weight, plus travel time, packing, stairs and other fees.
  4. For an interstate move, check the mover's USDOT number and registration with FMCSA before you sign.

Hold each mover's written estimate against the calculator's range, and ask about any line that falls outside it. That check is the surest way to know how much do movers cost for your own move before you sign.

Key takeaways

The main numbers on this page, in a few lines.

  • With 3 movers, a 2-bedroom home move takes about 4–6.5 hours on site: $720–$1,800 off peak at 10 road miles.
  • A 2-bedroom home move of 10 road miles, off peak: $58–$103 with a rental truck before help, $390–$1,380 with a container, and $720–$1,800 with full-service movers.
  • A 2-bedroom home move takes up about 640–930 cu ft: the smallest truck that holds the heavy end is 20 ft.
  • The moving checklist has 14 tasks, from 6 weeks before the move to after the move.
  • Tip guides suggest $4–$15 per mover per hour: $16–$98 per mover for 4–6.5 hours on site, $48–$294 for 3 movers.
  • Guides put a 2-bedroom home at about 40–90 boxes.
  • Local movers bill for the crew's time, so home size, stairs and access set most of the price.
  • Long-distance movers price by the weight of your shipment and the miles, not the hours.
  • A firm price needs a written estimate after an in-home or video survey of your belongings.
  • Ask which valuation option a price includes before you compare two movers.

Weeks-ahead tasks that keep the moving bill down

Much of how much do movers cost on the day depends on how ready you are. Work down these tasks, from booking parking to walking the crew through, so paid hours go on moving.

0 of 14 done

6 weeks before

  • Get every possible extra charge listed on the estimate, so the price you pay is the price you were given.

  • Know what it costs to change the date or cancel, and how much notice you must give.

  • Then compare it with the coverage the moving company offers.

4 weeks before

  • Whether it takes a deposit, when the rest is due, and which payment methods it accepts.

2 weeks before

  • A sketch with each room named lets the crew put things in place on the first trip.

  • Plan how those will travel, or give them away before moving day.

1 week before

  • Keys, gate or door codes, and someone there to let them in.

  • Chargers, basic tools, toilet paper, cleaning supplies, snacks and a change of clothes.

  • Ask the building or the city whether you need a permit or cones.

The day before

  • Take up rugs that slide, and protect floors where heavy pieces will roll.

  • Tape a sign on it, or gather it in one room, so it isn't loaded by mistake.

Moving day

  • Photograph each page if no copy is handed to you.

  • Point out anything fragile, very heavy or going to a particular room.

After the move

  • Send photos and a list of what's damaged or missing as soon as you find it.

Tips to plan on top of the price

Tips are not part of how much do movers cost in the calculator's estimate, so budget them separately. This works out what tipping guides suggest for each mover and for the whole crew.

3 movers 4–6.5 hours

Per mover $16–$98

For the crew $48–$294

Who to tip and when

  • Tipping is up to you: guides call a tip a thank-you for good work, not an obligation. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, This Old House and U-Haul)
  • Guides find cash simplest, handed to each mover at the end of the job. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, This Old House, MoveAdvisor and CNET)
  • When one crew loads and another unloads, guides suggest tipping each crew after it finishes its part. (HireAHelper, CNET, Real Simple, American Van Lines and NerdWallet)
  • On a move of several days, guides suggest tipping at the end of each day, in case the crew changes. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet and Forbes Home)
  • Guides suggest a separate tip for a separate packing crew. (CNET and This Old House)
  • Guides suggest asking the moving company about its tipping policy first: some build gratuity into the price, and some don't accept tips. (Forbes Home, This Old House and U-Haul)
  • Guides suggest tipping more for stairs, heavy furniture or bad weather, and less, or nothing, for damage, a late start or careless work. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, CNET and Real Simple)
  • Drinks and snacks are welcome, but guides don't count them as the tip. (NerdWallet and CNET)

Questions

How much do movers cost FAQ

Can't find your answer? Email hello@liftmyboxes.com.

How much should you budget for a move?

Start with how much do movers cost for your home size and distance, then add what sits outside that price: packing, supplies, tips and any storage. For a local 2-bedroom move, the movers' part is $720–$1,800 at 10 road miles, off peak, with no stairs or extras. Stairs or a summer date raise the range itself, so budget at the top of it or above.

What hidden fees can raise how much do movers cost?

The usual extras are stairs, a long carry from the door to the truck, an elevator, a shuttle truck where a big truck can't park, travel time and fuel. Packing materials, storage and full-value protection are priced separately too. Ask the mover to list every fee in the written estimate, so how much do movers cost on moving day matches what you agreed.

How much should you tip movers?

Tipping is up to you. Moving guides suggest a tip per mover for a half day or a full day, a larger daily tip for a long-distance crew, or a share of the bill. The tip calculator on this page works those published ranges out for your crew.

Is an online moving cost estimate the same as a quote?

No. An online estimate, like the calculator on this page, shows how much do movers cost for a move like yours. A firm price is the mover's written estimate, made after it has seen your belongings in person or by video. Use the online estimate to spot a mover's price that looks far too low or too high.
